item.text: {"text":"Temporal attention offers a plausible extension within BERT4Rec. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) learns pairwise time-interval representations alongside positional information, using historical timestamps without requiring the next interaction’s timestamp; borrow its temporal relations while retaining BERT4Rec’s bidirectional backbone. More recent work supports richer temporal modeling: [TLSTSRec](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) (online 2024; issue 2025) learns timestamp matrices capturing duration and time spectrum, with adaptive long-/short-term representations. [HyperHawkes](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) (WWW 2025) models repeated latent intents through Hawkes processes, motivating interest-dependent persistence rather than treating every older event as stale. These results do not establish gains for the pinned Amazon benchmark.\n\nConcrete hypothesis, inferred from these mechanisms: add jointly learned, per-head attention biases from bucketed log history-to-history time gaps, retaining content attention and positional embeddings. Different heads could learn persistent versus rapidly changing interests without deleting context or imposing universal monotonic decay. For the appended mask, use a learned unknown-time relation, optionally conditioned on each event’s age relative to the last observed interaction; never substitute the held-out target timestamp. Apply the same unknown-time treatment to masked training targets to prevent a timestamp shortcut unavailable at inference. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), reserved mask token, appended-mask inference, and final nonpadding readout. This remains one jointly trained BERT4Rec model per category; improved discrimination between repeated interests and stale events is an experimental hypothesis, not an established outcome."}
